transcript.text: I can speak to the remote participation issue from my perspective as outgoing chair. We've been running the monthly live sessions primarily from the main conference room, and I've noticed that when in-person attendees are having sidebar discussions or when we use physical whiteboards for brainstorming, the remote members on the video call struggle to follow along or jump in. The key participation moments where I've seen this happen are during open discussion segments and breakout activities — remote members often can't hear side conversations clearly, and they're left out of the visual collaboration. I think Priya's right that the new charter should include concrete commitments to address this, whether that's designating a remote-participation facilitator for each session or restructuring how we handle breakout discussions. I'd welcome hearing from any remote members on the line about their firsthand experience so we can make sure the charter commitments actually solve the problem.

transcript.text: I need to be specific about what I've observed. In 6 of the last 8 live sessions, remote members could not submit questions or vote because no one was monitoring the chat. That's the participation barrier I'm most concerned about — it's not just about hearing side conversations or following visual collaboration, though those are real issues too.
